cards.headline: Rod Stewart's hit cover sparked a feud with Bob Seger
cards.snippet: Singer Bob Seger recorded Tom Waits's "Downtown Train" in 1989. He says that on a trip to London he told Rod Stewart about his version, and a month later Stewart recorded it. Stewart's cover, released in late 1989, reached number three on the Billboard Hot 100. Stewart and his management deny that he took the idea from Seger. Seger dropped his plan to release the track in 1989 and re-recorded it in 2011.
cards.context: Seger shelved his version and re-recorded it in 2011.

cards.headline: The video features boxer Jake LaMotta
cards.snippet: The 1985 promo video for Tom Waits's "Downtown Train," from his album Rain Dogs, was shot in black and white. Jean-Baptiste Mondino directed it, and Andrea Ambandos produced it. It includes a cameo by the boxer Jake LaMotta.
cards.context: Filmed to promote the single from Rain Dogs (1985).

cards.headline: A moon that punches a hole in the night
cards.snippet: One Genius reading takes it as the best way to describe burning the midnight oil, working through the night. The mystical night gets "punched into like a punchclock."
cards.context: One fan calls it "one of the greatest opening lines EVER" and says this song and video introduced them to Tom Waits. They've been hooked since.

cards.headline: One line that sums up Waits
cards.snippet: Tom Waits writes songs about wounded people with just a few drops of dream left.

cards.headline: Serenade me every full moon
cards.snippet: I wouldn't mind Tom Waits singing outside my window every time there's a full moon
cards.context: Echoes the song's late-night, street-corner feel.

cards.headline: Uptown doorman vs. downtown paper bag
cards.snippet: Rod is singing from his terrace in his Uptown doorman building while drinking a glass of wine, and Tom is singing outside of his Downtown walk-up and drinking out of a paper bag.
cards.context: Contrasts Waits' original with Rod Stewart's polished hit cover.

cards.headline: A warning about Tom Waits
cards.snippet: "If you are listening to Tom Waits, it's already too late." - Some Dude.
